problems.stem: A facial-recognition model trained mostly on light-skinned faces performs worse on dark-skinned faces. Which bias source is the primary contributor?
options: Historical bias (the world has fewer dark-skinned people).
Representation bias — the training distribution does not match the deployment distribution across subgroups.
Aggregation bias — one model is being used for too many tasks.
There is no bias; the model is correct on average.
problems.explanation: Differential subgroup error driven by skewed training distribution is representation bias. The Gender Shades work (Buolamwini and Gebru) is the canonical example.

problems.stem: A healthcare risk model uses 'annual healthcare expenditure' as a proxy for 'healthcare need' and underestimates the need of one demographic group. What kind of bias is this?
options: Measurement bias — the proxy correlates with the target differently across groups, because the same need was historically met with less spending in some groups.
problems.explanation: When the same underlying state produces different observed values across groups, the proxy is measurement-biased. Obermeyer et al. (Science 2019) is the canonical case.

problems.stem: A predictive-policing system sends more patrols to neighborhoods predicted to be high-crime, which records more crime there, which trains the next model to predict more crime there. What kind of bias is this and what is the right intervention?
options: Deployment / feedback-loop bias. The system's own deployment manufactures the data that confirms it. Right intervention: counterfactual evaluation, randomized exploration to break the loop, periodic re-grounding against external truth.
problems.explanation: Self-confirming feedback loops are deployment-time bias. Retraining on more of the loop's own output is the trap; breaking the loop is the fix.

problems.stem: Which statement most accurately describes the limits of post-processing 'debiasing' techniques?
options: Post-processing can eliminate any bias regardless of source.

Post-processing can change which group bears which kind of error but cannot create information the model never had, rewrite the target variable, or break a deployment feedback loop. Some biases require non-engineering responses (target change, declining to deploy).
Post-processing is the same as data resampling.
Bias cannot be reduced at all.
problems.explanation: Post-processing reshuffles errors but cannot fix bias rooted in target choice, missing information, or feedback loops. The honest answer is that some interventions live outside engineering.
